newsitem.title: UK: Siebe squeezed up on talk of buy note.
newsitem.headline: Siebe squeezed up on talk of buy note.

text.p: Shares in Siebe Plc were up 24p to 10.38-1/2 stg, against a weaker market trend by 1325 GMT, after reports that a major broker had issued a buy recommendation on the engineering group, dealers said.
"Siebe is on several analysts' buy lists and it looks like one of them has reiterated a buy stance today," the head of trading at a large brokerage said.
Dealers said a shortage of stock also helped underpin the share price.
"There have been a few large buyers around in the market this morning and its been squeezed up," another dealer said.
"With the FTSE looking vulnerable, some people are looking for stocks with overseas exposure. Siebe fits the bill as a defensive play."
Around 45 percent of Siebe's revenues are derived from the U.S., with the Pacific region accounting for nearly 12 percent, according to data on Reuters Securities 3000.
Zafar Khan, analyst at SocGen said he had been a "fan" of Siebe for "a very long time" but now rated the stock as a hold.
"We think the stock is fairly valued," Khan said.
From March 20, 1996 to March 19, 1997, Siebe has outperformed the FTSE 100 index by around 3.5 percent and the FT Engineering Sector by 11 percent.

Siebe, which reported earnings per share of 45 pence for the full-year to 6 April 1996, is forecast to post earnings of 52.20 pence per share for the 12-months to March 31, 1997, and 59.90 pence per share to March 31, 1998, according to consensus estimates data on Reuters Securities 3000.
